chain.title: Glass and Sticks First
chain.desc: Eight glass around a stick, four at a time. The Window Base is the gate for this entire mod - almost every window in it takes a base as an ingredient, so nothing else can be built until you have one.

chain.title: Half the Bar
chain.desc: Shapeless from a Window Centre Bar Base, and back again. The two barred bases and the plain base are the three frames every window style is built on.

chain.title: The Cross Bar
chain.desc: Shapeless, two from a half bar base. It is the frame the four-pane windows use.

chain.title: A Window That Resizes
chain.desc: A window base ringed by logs, four at a time. The Resizeable Window is the mod's default; the Rectangle version uses the half bar base and the Four Pane version the centre bar base.

chain.title: Change Its Shape
chain.desc: An iron ingot, nuggets and a stick. The mod's hint is exact: 'Right click on a window, to change their shape'. It is the tool that makes one window id cover several silhouettes.

chain.title: Lock It Shut
chain.desc: A window base and iron nuggets on a diagonal. 'Right click on a window, to lock them' - the second tool, and the reason the jar ships an iron-bars-toggle sound.

chain.title: Thin, Not Deep
chain.desc: A window base ringed by logs, eight at a time. Pane windows are the flattest of the four window silhouettes and the widest family in the mod at 31 materials.

chain.title: Boards Over the Glass
chain.desc: Three trapdoors of the same wood in a column give three Shutters. The Louvered Shutter is the same column built from slabs instead, and it reaches into stone materials too.

chain.title: Slats You Can Close
chain.desc: Sticks over two rows of slabs, three at a time. The jar ships open and close sounds for them, so blinds are interactive rather than static.

chain.title: Something to Hang It From
chain.desc: A stick between two logs, five at a time. Golden and metal rods use ingots and nuggets instead.

chain.title: Cloth on the Rod
chain.desc: Two wool of one colour, three at a time. Curtains come in all sixteen colours and need a rod to hang on.

chain.title: Patterned Panes
chain.desc: Eight stained glass of one colour around a dye of the same colour, eight at a time. Mosaic glass and its panes are sixteen colours each and are the only glass this mod adds that is not a window.

chain.title: See Out, Not In
chain.desc: Six glass and three black dye, six at a time. One-way glass and its pane are the mod's only functional glass and have no colour variants.

chain.title: A Low Wall for the Ledge
chain.desc: Stone over stone and a stick, five at a time. Parapets run stone, log and plank versions and are the balcony rail rather than a window.

chain.title: A Slot to Shoot Through
chain.desc: Stone and slabs in a narrow column, three at a time. Eight arrow slits, all stone, all castle.

chain.title: The Pointed Arch
chain.desc: Glass panes in a diamond of stone, four at a time. Seven Gothic Windows, one per brick type.

chain.title: Iron Instead of Wood
chain.desc: A window base ringed by iron blocks. The metal window, its rectangle, four-pane and pane versions are the only windows in the mod built from a metal block.

notes: MACAW'S MODS SHARE ONE STRUCTURE: A SMALL NUMBER OF DISTINCT BLOCK TYPES CROSSED WITH A LARGE MATERIAL TABLE. The chain below is one step per distinct RECIPE SHAPE, not one per id, and the material tables go to wheels. MODDB: no consensus signal - moddb.json contains no key for any Macaw's mod - so every ordering here is the recipe graph alone and there is no conflict to record. Verified against mcw-mcwwindows-2.4.2-mc1.20.1forge.jar as shipped in this pack. ID DETECTION AND WIDENING - THIS IS THE INVERTED-NAMING JAR OF THE MACAW'S SET: 326 item models, 328 blockstates, 315 lang block./item. keys; models INTERSECT lang = 315, the count used, and all 315 have a recipe. NARROWED for 11 model-only stems, and the reason is a naming mismatch worth recording: the registered log windows are spelled stripped_<wood>_LOG_window, but the jar ALSO ships item models named stripped_<wood>_window with the _log_ dropped, for acacia, birch, cherry, crimson, dark oak, jungle, mangrove, oak, spruce and warped. Those ten have no lang key, no blockstate, no recipe and no loot table; the real ids are the _log_ spellings, which do have all four. The eleventh, window_bar, is a shared model part. WIDENING REJECTED for 18 blockstate-only stems: crimson_window, crimson_window2, crimson_four_window, crimson_plank_window, crimson_plank_window2, crimson_plank_four_window, stripped_crimson_log_window / _window2 / _four_window and the nine matching warped entries. Each has a blockstate pointing at a model under models/block/window_barred/ but no item model, no lang key, no recipe and no loot table, while the registered crimson and warped windows are spelled crimson_STEM_window and warped_STEM_window and do have all four. These are leftovers from the pre-1.16 stem naming. Between the two directions, 29 plausible-looking stems are excluded and the intersection is exactly right. THE GATE THAT MAKES THIS MOD A CHAIN: mcwwindows:window_base is an ingredient in nearly every window recipe in the jar, and window_half_bar_base and window_centre_bar_base convert into each other shapelessly and gate the Rectangle and Four Pane silhouettes respectively. No window can be made before the base, which is a genuine prerequisite rather than a flat table. TWO TOOLS: mcwwindows.hammer.desc = 'Right click on a window, to change their shape' and mcwwindows.key.desc = 'Right click on a window, to lock them'. The jar also ships open/close subtitles for windows, blinds and iron bars, so this mod's blocks are the most interactive of the Macaw's set after the fences. DISTINCT BLOCK TYPES: 51 name-stems, about 15 real shapes. Verified yields: window_base 4, window 4, window2 8, four_window 8, pane_window 8, shutter 3, louvered_shutter 3, blinds 3, curtain_rod 5, curtain 3, mosaic_glass 8, one_way_glass 6, parapet 5, arrow_slit 3, gothic 4, hammer 1, key 1. DROPS: the 10 stripped_<wood>_window orphan models, window_bar, and the 18 crimson/warped blockstate leftovers.
